NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks time-based filter replacement (90-day schedule). My observable is the filter's effective dust-holding capacity depletion rate, inferred from the changing relationship between fan power and pressure drop. This departure captures the actual filter loading physics rather than assuming constant accumulation rate, as the pressure drop increases non-linearly with dust loading while fan power responds to both pressure drop and system resistance changes.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔP = k·v^m·c, where ΔP is pressure drop, v is air velocity, c is dust concentration, and m is typically 1.5-2.0 for pleated filters. Fan power P ∝ ΔP·v. The depletion rate is dc/dt ∝ (ΔP_observed - ΔP_clean)/t. A filter with 50% remaining capacity would show ΔP at 25-50% of final value (for m=1.5), not 50%. This non-linear relationship is the key physics standard practice ignores.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) BMS data historian (existing), 2) Standard Python/Excel processing (off-the-shelf), 3) Time-series analysis library (SciPy, open source). Procedure: 1) Log daily ΔP and fan power during occupied hours, 2) Calculate daily ΔP/fan_power ratio, 3) Fit exponential decay curve to this ratio over time, 4) When decay rate exceeds threshold (20% faster than initial), trigger replacement alert. All computation uses existing BMS points with standard math.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: SAME (uses existing points). Operability: SAME (triggers same replacement workflow). Maintenance: SAME (no new equipment). Cost class: SAME (computation cost negligible vs filter savings). Expected conclusion: 20%+ reduction in unnecessary replacements while preventing overloaded operation, with no additional operational burden.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install new filter, log daily ΔP and fan power for 180 days. Instruments: Existing BMS sensors. Pass threshold: Alert triggered within 7 days when filter reaches 80% loading (verified by manual measurement), with <5 false positives in 180 days. Kill criterion: Alert doesn't trigger at 80% loading, or triggers before 60% loading, or has >10 false positives. Duration: 180-day test with 3 filter cycles.
